title: Victorian runoff losses after 1997 were largest where shallow water tables fell below their rainfall relation, but water tables did not track runoff year to year (419 bores, 1975-2021)
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian runoff stayed 20-25% below its 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation. Did groundwater also change, and does it explain the runoff loss? Approach: we used 3,410 Victorian bores (DEECA WMIS) and CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments. For 419 bores within 5 km of a catchment, we fitted the annual water-table level on an exponentially weighted rain anomaly for years up to 1996. We compared the 2010-2021 residuals with runoff deficits from the annual model Q = a + bP + cP(t-1) + dT fitted on 1951-1996, with AGCD and SILO rain. We wrote the plan before we compared bores with runoff. Results: in 2010-2021, the median shallow bore was 1.00 m below its rainfall relation (95% CI 0.42-1.95 m; 87% of bores below). It stayed low in wet years. A pre-1997 placebo gave -0.08 m. The planned cross-catchment test (30 or more calibration years, n = 24) was inconclusive (Spearman rho 0.31, -0.15 to 0.78). With 20 or more years (amendment, n = 46), larger water-table shortfalls went with larger runoff deficits (rho 0.49, 0.06 to 0.69, AGCD; 0.56, 0.15 to 0.75, SILO). Where the shortfall was 2 m or more, runoff was about 50% below the relation. Where it was less than 0.5 m, the deficit was -21% with AGCD rain but -3% (-14 to +3%) with SILO rain. The water table did not act as a storage state: a water-table index in the 1975-1996 runoff model changed the median deficit only from -16% to -14%. Within catchments, year-to-year water-table changes did not track the runoff residual (-0.4% per m, -5.7 to +3.4). The loss of rain sensitivity did not follow the water table. Faster recessions (bundle 7cecffa9) went with larger shortfalls (rho -0.31, all bores). Conclusion: the water-table shortfall marks where runoff was lost, but it does not set runoff as a linear store. A threshold disconnection or a common loss before recharge agree with the data. Limitations: Victoria only; bores are not at streams; pumping is not known; short pre-1997 bore records; the main link test uses an amended calibration rule.
